<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Mopti attacks]]
***Four [[Malian Armed Forces|Malian troops]] are killed and 12 others wounded when their anti-[[poaching]] convoy is [[ambush]]ed in [[Mopti Region|Mopti]]. [[Islamist]] [[insurgent]]s are suspected to be behind the attack and reinforcements are sent to the area from [[Konna]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mali-security-attack/militants-kill-four-malian-soldiers-in-ambush-idUSKBN25N2GM?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**Four civilians in [[2020 Afghanistan flood|flooded]] [[Parwan Province|Parwan]] are killed in clashes between the [[Afghan military]] and the [[Taliban]]. The group did not comment on the killings ahead of [[Afghan peace process|peace talks]] to start soon between the group and the [[government of Afghanistan|government]]. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-08-27/taliban-fighters-reportedly-kill-civilians-in-flood-afghanistan/12604414 (ABC Australia)]
*[[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen]]
**The [[Saudi Arabia]]n-led coalition says it has intercepted a [[ballistic missile]] fired at the Saudi city of [[Najran]] from [[Yemen]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-saudi-security-houthi/saudi-led-coalition-intercepts-a-ballistic-missile-launched-towards-najran-idUKKBN25N305?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]], [[economy of South Korea]]
**The [[Bank of Korea]] cuts its growth forecast and expects the country's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] to shrink 1.3% this year. It would be South Korea's worst performance since the height of the [[1997 Asian financial crisis|Asian financial crisis]] in 1998. [https://www.marketwatch.com/story/bank-of-korea-maintains-rate-cuts-growth-outlook-2020-08-26 (Marketwatch)]
*[[China–United States trade war]]
**American retailer [[Walmart]] announces its partnership with [[Microsoft]] for a bid to acquire the Chinese-based [[Online video platform|video sharing service]] [[TikTok]], which faces a ban in the United States through [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s [[List of executive actions by Donald Trump|executive order]] if its parent company [[ByteDance]] fails to sell the app's operations to an American corporation. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/world/1975743/walmart-says-teaming-with-microsoft-in-bid-for-tiktok (AFP via ''Bangkok Post'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Laura]] downgrades from a Category 4 to Category 2 [[hurricane]] but remains "extremely dangerous" after lashing the coasts of [[Texas]] and [[Louisiana]] early Thursday. It has killed 30 people thus far. [https://apnews.com/45ba32bafe5da34b5691544ecb3e5492 (AP)]
**A shelter-in-place is issued after a chemical fire breaks out in [[Lake Charles, Louisiana]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/chemical-plant-fire-lake-charles-louisiana-hurricane-laura-wake/ (CBS News)]
**The South's Defenders Monument, a [[Confederate States of America|Confederate]] monument located in Lake Charles, is damaged by Laura. [https://thehill.com/changing-america/respect/diversity-inclusion/513973-hurricane-laura-topples-confederate-monument (''The Hill'')]
*Ten teenagers in [[Arua]], [[Uganda]], are killed after being struck by [[lightning]] while playing [[Association football|football]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53947117 (BBC News)] [https://www.softpower.ug/dark-evening-as-lightning-strikes-8-teenagers-dead-in-arua/ (Soft Power News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] reports 441 new cases in the last 24 hours, the highest single-day increase of confirmed cases since early March, as sporadic cluster infections across the country, mainly in the [[Seoul Capital Area]], continue to pile up, fueling calls for tougher antivirus restrictions. [https://news.detik.com/internasional/d-5148751/rekor-tertinggi-sejak-maret-korsel-catat-441-kasus-corona-sehari (AP via detikNews)] [https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/east-asia/article/3099029/coronavirus-south-korea-records-most-new-cases-march-raising (''South China Morning Post'')]
****The [[National Assembly (South Korea)|National Assembly]] temporarily closes and a group of more than ten [[Democratic Party (South Korea, 1955)|Democratic Party]] officials, including the party chairman [[Lee Hae-chan]] and parliamentary leader [[Kim Tae-nyeon]], undergo screening tests and are placed in self-quarantine after a [[Photojournalism|photojournalist]] covering a meeting of the ruling party tested positive for COVID-19. [https://www.euronews.com/2020/08/27/south-korea-shuts-parliament-after-photographer-tests-positive-for-covid-19 (Euronews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****The number of deaths in [[India]] surpasses 60,000 as the country reports its highest single day record of more than 75,000 new cases in the last 24 hours. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/india-records-highest-ever-single-day-spike-of-over-75-000-covid-19-cases-tally-above-3-3-million/story-Qi5X9QSIYpipVVQ6iwBy4J.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports 2,719 new cases in the last 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total to 162,884. This is the highest single-day rise since the beginning of the outbreak. Additionally, the total death toll surpasses 7,000. [https://jakartaglobe.id/news/indonesia-reports-recordbreaking-daily-count-of-coronavirus (Jakarta Globe)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[Prime Minister of France|Prime Minister]] [[Jean Castex]] announces the mandatory wearing of [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|face masks]] throughout [[Paris]] after officials released statistics indicating a resurgence of cases throughout the country. [https://today.rtl.lu/news/world/a/1570904.html (AFP via RTL Today)]
****[[France]] records its highest number of new daily infections since the end of the lockdown in early May, with an additional 6,111 cases reported over the past 24 hours, making it the second highest ever, after 7,578 new cases set on March 30. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53934952 (BBC News)] [https://www.france24.com/en/20200827-france-records-more-than-6-000-new-covid-19-cases-highest-figure-since-april (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] records its highest number of new cases since early May, when the country was still in lockdown, with 1,411 new cases reported in the last 24 hours. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2020/08/27/italy-records-highest-number-coronavirus-cases-since-lockdown/amp/ (''The Telegraph'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]	
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Alabama]]	
****[[List of governors of Alabama|Alabama Governor]] [[Kay Ivey]] extends the state's [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandate]] and [[Stay-at-home order|safer-at-home order]] to October 2. [https://www.bizjournals.com/birmingham/news/2020/08/27/safer-at-home-extended-until-october.html (Bizjournals.com)] [https://patch.com/alabama/birmingham-al/ivey-extends-mask-order-october (Patch.com)]
*[[Fiji]]'s opposition parties condemn the [[government of Fiji|government]] over the handling of the [[dengue fever]] and [[leptospirosis]] outbreaks, saying that the government has not informed the public of the seriousness of the diseases. [[Vice-president]] of the [[National Federation Party]] (NFP) [[Lenora Qereqeretabua]] says that the government needs to urgently develop a plan and also condemns what she considers is a mishandling of [[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji|COVID-19]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/424537/fiji-govt-doing-nothing-about-dengue-leptospirosis-opposition-says (RNZ)]

;International relations
*[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Czech Republic]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Jamaica]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland]]
***The British government removes [[Switzerland]], the [[Czech Republic]], and [[Jamaica]] from the travel corridor list due to rising COVID-19 infection rates. It means that arrivals from those countries will have to self-quarantine for two weeks, [[Secretary of State for Transport|Transport Secretary]] [[Grant Shapps]] confirmed. The change will come into effect on Saturday at 4:00 a.m. [[British Summer Time|BST]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/travel/2020/aug/27/england-may-remove-switzerland-and-jamaica-from-travel-corridor-list (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Colombia–United States relations]]
**[[Colombia]]n Defense Minister [[Carlos Holmes Trujillo]] permits a [[United States Army|U.S. Army]] unit to resume its advisory mission in the country after the [[Senate of Colombia|Colombian Senate]] found that it did not constitute a deployment of foreign troops. A court had suspended the mission in early July after the opposition argued it did count as foreign troop movement, and thus needed Senate authorization. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-colombia-usa/colombia-says-visiting-us-military-unit-to-restart-activities-idUSKBN25N2JT (Reuters)]
*[[Egypt–Greece relations]]
**The [[Hellenic Parliament]] formally ratifies a maritime agreement with [[Egypt]], that defines maritime boundaries and an [[exclusive economic zone]] between the two countries in the [[Mediterranean Sea]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-greece-egypt-parliament-turkey/greek-parliament-ratifies-maritime-accord-with-egypt-idUSKBN25N2M2 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[Poisoning of Alexei Navalny (2020)|Poisoning of Alexei Navalny]]
**[[Police of Russia|Russian police]] launch a preliminary investigation into the suspected poisoning of opposition figure [[Alexei Navalny]] on August 20 to determine whether to open a [[criminal investigation]]. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/europe/russian-police-launch-initial-check-into-navalny-case/articleshow/77782333.cms (AFP via ''The Times of India'')]
*[[Christchurch mosque shootings]]
**[[Australia]]n Brenton Harrison Tarrant is sentenced to [[Life imprisonment in New Zealand|life imprisonment]] without possibility of [[parole]], a first in [[History of New Zealand|New Zealand history]], for killing 51 people in last year's [[mass shooting]]s at two mosques in [[Christchurch]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/27/christchurch-shooting-mosque-gunman-sentenced-to (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2020 Malian coup d'état]]
**Ousted [[President of Mali|Malian President]] [[Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta]] is freed by military authorities, a military junta spokesman informs. "He was freed this morning, [and] he has returned to his home", said the spokesman without elaborating. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mali-security/ousted-mali-president-keita-has-been-freed-by-coup-leaders-says-junta-spokesman-idUSKBN25N1US (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**Police in [[Belarus]] arrest 20 journalists who were planning to cover a protest in [[Minsk]] and confiscated their telephones and identity documents. The interior ministry later said that the journalists had been driven to the police station to check they had valid accreditation allowing them to work as journalists. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/belarus-detains-journalists-anti-gov-protest-minsk-200827155127123.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Delta Air Lines]] has banned 240 passengers for refusing to wear masks since a policy requiring them went into effect in June. [https://www.cnn.com/travel/article/delta-airlines-no-fly-list-tops-240/index.html (CNN)]
*At least three people are killed when a feud between [[Hezbollah]] supporters and a local clan of [[Sunni]] [[Arab]]s ends with gunfight in south [[Beirut]], Lebanon. The army arrives at the scene and arrests four people. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2020/08/27/Clashes-in-Beirut-s-southern-town-of-Khaldeh-erupts-between-local-tribes-Hezbollah.html (Al Arabiya English)]
*[[Law enforcement in the Netherlands|Dutch police]] report that ''[[Two Laughing Boys with a Mug of Beer]]'', a painting by [[Dutch Golden Age painting|Dutch golden age painter]] [[Frans Hals]], was stolen from the [[Hofje van Mevrouw van Aerden]] in [[Leerdam]]. This is the third time the painting had been stolen. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-netherlands-art-frans-hals-theft/frans-hals-painting-two-laughing-boys-stolen-for-a-third-time-idUSKBN25N1WA?il=0 (Reuters)]
*The [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] arrests [[Yaser Abdel Said]], who had been on their [[FBI Ten Most Wanted Fugitives|Ten Most Wanted Fugitives]] list since 2014 for allegedly murdering his two daughters in an [[honor killing]] in 2008. His son and brother were also arrested for harboring a fugitive. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-53934168 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Afghan peace process]]
**[[Abdullah Abdullah]], chairman of the High Council for National Reconciliation, says that peace talks between the [[Taliban]] and the government will start in September with the support of the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]], which pushes both sides to set differences aside. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/world/2020/08/27/Afghan-officials-Taliban-to-start-peace-talks-in-September.html (Al Arabiya)]
*[[Kurds|Kurdish]] human rights lawyer [[Ebru Timtik]] dies in hospital after spending 238-days on [[hunger strike]] in protest of her imprisonment after being found guilty of being a member of the outlawed [[Revolutionary People's Liberation Party/Front]]. At the time of her death, she was reported to only weigh 65 pounds. [https://nypost.com/2020/08/29/ebru-timtik-dies-after-238-day-hunger-strike/ (''New York Post'')]
